title: India proposes Indo-Pacific ocean data exchange and maritime AI network to spot suspicious ships
dek: Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh closed the Navy's Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue with four proposals, including a shared cloud platform for small island states, reports said.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India has proposed a shared cloud platform for Indo-Pacific countries to pool ocean data and a regional network of artificial intelligence centres to track shipping, including the "shadow fleet" tankers that carry sanctioned oil, Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh said at the close of the Indian Navy's annual Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue in New Delhi on Thursday, according to reports.

The three-day conference, run by the Navy with the National Maritime Foundation, ended with a focus on "cooperative ocean governance and responsible maritime technologies", the Defence Ministry said. It drew more than 40 experts and speakers from 20 countries under the theme "Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific".

## The four proposals

Mr Singh set out four areas of cooperation in his valedictory address, according to one report of the speech; the ministry's release names him as the speaker but does not give the text.

- An Indo-Pacific ocean data exchange: a multilateral cloud platform where member states could share and use non-sensitive oceanographic, seabed, tidal and weather data. Small island states that cannot afford satellites or research vessels could use it to watch their exclusive economic zones, track illegal fishing and manage coastal erosion. "By pooling our data, we can democratize maritime domain awareness," he said, according to the report.
- A regional maritime AI network linking research centres to build open-source models that tell legitimate shipping from suspicious movements, including shadow-fleet tankers. He called for algorithmic transparency and human oversight so that such systems follow international humanitarian law and do not cause accidental escalation.
- A marine pollution early-warning system combining satellite imagery with autonomous coastal vessels carrying chemical sensors, to produce public maps of contamination and illegal extraction.
- A fellowship for scholars, naval officers and doctoral students, jointly funded by India and its partners, modelled on the Rhodes and Fulbright scholarships.

He described India's Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative of 2019, on which the plans would build, as "not a military pact" but an open platform, and said rivalry now extends beneath the surface to undersea cables, the report said.

## What other speakers said

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the conference on Wednesday that "the global maritime security environment is strained by deliberate trade disruptions", and spoke of "blatant challenges to the freedom of navigation and the weaponisation of narrow maritime passages", according to the ministry's release. He did not name any country. The Chief of Naval Staff, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, called for collective investment in ocean science, data sharing and joint scientific expeditions, the ministry said.

Opening the dialogue on Tuesday, Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi (retired), the former Navy chief who now chairs the National Maritime Foundation, said disruptions in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz had shown the cost of instability in confined waters, and pointed to continuing tensions in the South China Sea, reports said.

## Why it matters

The proposals put data and technology, rather than warships, at the centre of India's offer to smaller Indian Ocean and Pacific states, many of which are also courted by China with ports, loans and research vessels. Shadow-fleet tankers have become a security concern in the Indian Ocean since the Iran war began, and earlier this week the US sanctioned a Chandigarh-based network accused of selling false flag registrations to Iran's tankers.

The ideas build on existing arrangements such as the Navy's Information Fusion Centre for the Indian Ocean Region in Gurugram and the Quad's Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness, both discussed at the conference. No timetable, cost or list of partner countries for the new platforms has been announced.
